solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One tucking in tucks it in

definitions.text: One tucking in tucks it in

parts.words: One tucking in tucks it in
parts.note: someone tucking into a meal tucks a cloth into their collar to protect their clothes

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone who tucks things in while tucking in.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'tucking in' means eating heartily; the second 'tucks it in' is literal, pushing a cloth into a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A table linen square is what a diner tucks under the chin while eating.

clue.text: Make known it's not provided before end of May

parts.note: taken as written
provided, as in 'provided that', means if

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word May

explanation.surface: A note saying something isn't supplied until late May.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone formally is to make a thing known to them.

clue.text: Agitated Rupert wrecked place of retirement

indicators.note: wrecked means the name Rupert is smashed up and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: bed is where one retires for the night

explanation.surface: An upset Rupert has ruined the place he retired to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges RUPERT to PERTUR; 'place of retirement' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disturbed and anxious is agitated; both are synonyms for being upset.

clue.text: In former USSR, capping gold tooth

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece capping another sits on top of it, so it comes first

parts.note: taken as written
the CIS, Commonwealth of Independent States, succeeded the USSR
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone in the old Soviet Union gets a gold crown on a tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capping' puts CIS above OR in this down answer; dental capping is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tooth at the front of the mouth is one kind of tooth.

clue.text: Launch is cancelled after reprimand

indicators.note: after places the word for cancelled behind the word for reprimand

parts.note: to blast someone is to reprimand them fiercely
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: A rocket launch is scrubbed after someone gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch' reads as part of the news story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket's departure from the pad is its launch, a noun sense.

clue.text: The Parisian with a new list

parts.note: le is French for 'the', as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A Frenchman produces a fresh list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' means a tilt, as a ship lists, not a written roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lists tilts to one side, so to list is to lean over.

clue.text: Itch in one's cab, ie scratchy

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone notices an itch while sitting in a scratchy taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'one'S CAB, IE Scratchy'; 'scratchy' looks like a mix-up signal but supplies the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin infestation by mites is known colloquially as the itch.

clue.text: Bloomer with neat outer edge

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a lip is the rim or outer edge of something

explanation.surface: A gaffe made by someone with a tidy fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a mistake but is a flowering plant; 'neat' is not tidy but the archaic word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: This primula is a wild flower, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Feel dirt removed could be strained

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters shifted, and could be says they might form another word

explanation.surface: Dirt that is felt and taken away might have been sieved out.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid passed through a sieve or filter has been strained.

clue.text: Now and again, once more after that

definitions.text: Now and again, once more after that

parts.words: Now and again, once more after that
parts.note: now is one time, again a second, and once more after that a third

explanation.surface: A vague phrase about doing something occasionally and then repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and again' looks like 'occasionally' but is counted as one time plus a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on three occasions means doing it three times.

clue.text: Meeting's impossible in bars like this

definitions.text: Meeting's impossible in bars like this

parts.words: Meeting's impossible in bars like this
parts.note: lines running side by side never meet, and gymnasts use bars of this kind

explanation.surface: A complaint that pubs of a certain kind are hopeless for getting together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs, but it is the gymnastic apparatus with two rails that never touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or rails that run side by side at constant distance never meet.

clue.text: Unhesitant ruler had very good turn in the big shops

indicators.note: unhesitant means without the hesitation sound er, so those letters go

parts.note: an emperor is a ruler

indicators.note: turn says the expression for very good is read back to front

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or very good; the 1 is written as I

explanation.surface: A decisive monarch took a fine stroll around the department stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhesitant' strips ER (a hesitation) from EMPEROR to leave EMPOR; 'turn' reverses A1 to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporium means a large store, and this is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Reportedly in favour of any small group

indicators.note: reportedly signals that what follows is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: being in favour of something is being for it; some can stand for any, as in 'have you any' or 'have you some'

explanation.surface: Apparently support for any small group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns 'for some' into a word sounding just like it.
explanation.definitionFit: A party of four people, as at golf or bridge, is a small group.

clue.text: Behind some asparagus one leaves pale drink

indicators.note: behind places the shortened pale after the piece of asparagus

parts.note: an asparagus tip is a part of the vegetable

indicators.note: leaves means the letter standing for one departs from the word pale

parts.note: taken as written
A is used for one, as the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tip-off about asparagus leaves leading to a pale beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage but is a verb: A (one) leaves PALE to give PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink that someone habitually enjoys is their favourite tipple.

clue.text: Clothes appear ragged on lecturer

indicators.note: ragged means the word appear is torn up and its letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: A lecturer turns up in tatty clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments worn on the body are collectively called clothes or attire.

clue.text: One who likes to make flying visits?

definitions.text: One who likes to make flying visits?

parts.words: One who likes to make flying visits?
parts.note: a migrating bird literally flies in and out, and the phrase also names a restless traveller

explanation.surface: A question about someone fond of brief drop-in calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying visits' are hasty calls, but read literally they are migrations on the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A migratory bird, or by extension a person who never settles anywhere long.

clue.text: Safe to fly dignitary from said Scottish resort first

indicators.note: first puts the sounded resort ahead of the dignitary
said signals that the resort's name is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: Ayr is a seaside town on Scotland's west coast
a worthy is a notable or dignified local person

explanation.surface: A dignitary declares a Scottish holiday town fit for flying.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a seaside town on Scotland's south-west coast; 'dignitary' is a local worthy, a dated term for a notable person.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft certified fit to fly is in safe flying condition.

clue.text: I agree to receive information twice

indicators.note: twice says the word for receiving information is written two times

parts.note: to hear news is to receive information

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing to be briefed two times over.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated cry is the traditional British parliamentary shout of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled cry is an exclamation of agreement, as used in Parliament.

clue.text: It's the last thing a tragedy is expected to do

definitions.text: It's the last thing a tragedy is expected to do

parts.words: It's the last thing a tragedy is expected to do
parts.note: a stage tragedy's final act is expected to finish with catastrophe

explanation.surface: Suggests a tragedy should never be predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last thing' seems to mean 'least likely', but literally it is how the play finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragic play conventionally concludes with ruin, so it finishes catastrophically.

clue.text: Any thug turned out to be disobedient

indicators.note: turned out says the letters of any thug are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A young thug proved to be unruly.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved child is naughty, a synonym for disobedient.

clue.text: Solicitor coming round may be less reserved

indicators.note: coming round says the word for solicitor wraps around another piece

parts.note: a tout is one who solicits custom, such as a ticket tout
may is the hawthorn, whose fruit is the haw

explanation.surface: A lawyer visiting might relax a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer but is a TOUT; 'may' looks like a verb but is the hawthorn tree, HAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To thaw out figuratively is to relax and become friendlier, less reserved.

clue.text: Some extra derequisitioning done by merchant

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dealer handles some extra property being released from requisition.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'done by merchant' as the definition, but 'merchant' alone means the answer; 'done by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer who buys and sells goods is a merchant.

clue.text: Strange Manx cat causing disturbance

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: An odd tailless cat from the Isle of Man stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx cats are naturally tailless, so 'Manx' docks the end of PUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy uproar or commotion is a disturbance.

clue.text: You are said to be featured in short man's picture

indicators.note: featured in says one piece appears inside another
short means the word for man loses its last letter

parts.note: male means man, the possessive adding nothing

indicators.note: said signals that the spoken words you are give letters that sound the same

parts.note: the two letters U and R, spoken, sound like 'you are'

explanation.surface: You appear in a small man's painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' means drop the last letter; 'said' tells you to hear 'You are' as two letters spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting applied directly to a wall is a large picture.

clue.text: Live, work — flog to death!

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
labour means work

explanation.surface: An exasperated motto about living, working and overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flog to death' is the idiom for going on about something far too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour a point excessively is to flog it to death, an idiom.

clue.text: Stitched all ways

parts.note: south is one of the four compass points covering every direction
east is another of the compass points
west is another of the compass points
north completes the set of compass points

explanation.surface: Sewn up in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all ways' means every direction: the four compass points, taken in an unusual order.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined with needle and thread means stitched.

clue.text: Burrow that is right to be less refined

parts.note: an earth is the burrow of a fox
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A fox's burrow is right to be coarser.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthier means cruder or more down-to-earth, so less refined.

clue.text: Unruly lot entered plot and took flight

indicators.note: entered says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: unruly means the letters of lot are out of order

explanation.surface: A rowdy group trespassed on land and then ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a scheme but is a garden bed, and the rowdy 'lot' is just letters to rearrange inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run off suddenly, so to have taken flight.

clue.text: Broadcasting about egg production

parts.note: re means about or concerning
hens produce eggs by laying

explanation.surface: Media coverage on the subject of poultry output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' means relaying a signal onward.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaying a programme means passing it on, retransmitting it, broadcasting it.

clue.text: Perhaps guest's one with lasting qualities

definitions.meaning: a guest is an example of one who stays somewhere
a horse or runner with stamina who keeps going over long distances

explanation.surface: A guest is said to have staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a guest as one example of somebody who stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are someone who stays: a visitor, or a competitor with endurance.
